title: 14-15. HE WILL SUBMIT TO FORCED LABOUR

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Issachar is a rawboned donkey lying down among the sheep pens. When he sees how good is his resting place and how pleasant is his land, he will bend his shoulder to the burden and submit to forced labour.'" — Gen 49:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Issachar is a strong donkey — capable, powerful, useful. And he lies down among the sheep pens because the land is pleasant and the resting place is good.

The picture is of strength surrendered for comfort. Issachar sees how nice the settled life is and accepts servitude rather than fight for freedom. He trades liberty for ease.

That is a temptation with a very modern face. Not dramatic sin, but slow settling. We are capable of far more than we do, and comfort is so pleasant that we bend our shoulders to burdens we should never have accepted. Debt taken on for things we did not need. Compromises made to keep a comfortable position. Convictions quietly parked because holding them costs too much.

Nobody wakes up and decides to give up their freedom. It happens by preferring the pleasant resting place, one small choice at a time.

Paul wrote that it was for freedom Christ set us free, and urged believers not to be burdened again by a yoke of slavery (Gal 5:1). That freedom must be actively kept.

Ask yourself honestly what comfort is currently costing you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What comfort might be quietly costing you more than you realise?
2. Where have you settled for less than God made you for?
3. Is there a burden you have accepted that was never yours to carry?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from trading what You have given me for what is merely comfortable. Show me where I have settled, and give me courage to live free in Christ. Amen.
